task.name: One data-backed model catalog on a single schema, replacing registry literals and models.custom
task.story_text:
## Why

Model definitions live in two places on two schemas. The shipped default set is Python literals in
the config package; project-declared models use a separate mapping that cannot express capability
or phase eligibility and derives them from tier instead. A third, fully expressive form exists for
inline entries in the enabled list.

Nothing about a model definition is behaviour — each is identity plus routing policy plus endpoint
and cost metadata. What genuinely requires code is the adapter that reaches a provider, because a
provider needs a runner module. That line is already the intended one, but the default model set
currently sits on the code side of it, which is why adding or re-pinning a model that runs on an
existing adapter requires a release, and why the two sources have drifted apart.

## Acceptance criteria

- The shipped default model set loads from data through the same parser that reads
  project-declared models, so both sources produce identical structures and one schema governs
  them.
- Declaring or re-pinning a model that runs on an already-supported adapter requires no code
  change and no release.
- A definition can express identity, transport, tier, capability, cost band, dev capability, phase
  eligibility, endpoint, and cost seeds; no field expressible in the shipped set is inexpressible
  in a project-declared one.
- Adding a provider that has no adapter continues to require code, and attempting to declare one
  in data fails with a message naming the supported adapters.
- Where a project declaration and a shipped definition describe the same canonical identity, the
  resolved entry reports which source supplied each field.
- Configuration written in the format this project uses today continues to load unchanged, so
  adopting the new schema is optional rather than forced by this change landing.
- This change does not rewrite the project's own configuration file. Moving that file onto the new
  schema is separate operator work, sequenced after a release containing this change has been cut
  and deployed, because the process that runs sprints for this repository is an installed release
  rather than the working tree and cannot read a schema it does not yet contain.

## Example

The same model is currently expressible three different ways with three different capabilities:

```
shipped default   _entry("openai", "gpt-5.4", "cli", tier=..., capability=9, phases=...)
                    → full expressiveness, requires a release to change

models.custom     openai/gpt-5.5/cli: {provider, model, transport, tier, input_cost_per_mtok}
                    → no capability, no phase_eligibility; capability derived from tier

enabled inline    {provider, model, transport, routing:{...}, cost:{...}, base_url}
                    → full expressiveness, but a selection list is not a definition surface
```

After this change one of these shapes exists, and the shipped set is expressed in it. Configuration
already written in the other shapes still loads.

handoff.summary: Moved the shipped model set out of Python literals into packaged data (src/theforge/config/data/models.yaml) written in a single canonical model-definition schema, and introduced src/theforge/config/model_catalog.py as the one parser for it. The parser splits into syntax validation (parse_definition — which is also where adapter validation happens, via transport_for) and two resolution modes: resolve_packaged (complete routing policy required, cost-band attribution enforced, used for the shipped catalog) and resolve_project (overlay onto a built-in of the same canonical identity, recording per-field provenance). config/models.py now builds AGENT_REGISTRY by loading that catalog through the shared parser, and its _entry() keyword helper is a thin adapter over the same parser so the two spellings cannot drift. In config/load.py the legacy models.custom flat mapping and inline models.enabled mapping became compatibility adapters that translate into the canonical shape before hitting the shared parser — including provider alias tokens (openai-api/gemini-cli) and declaration-key selection. Project declarations gained every field the shipped set could express (capability, phase_eligibility, cost_rank_basis, explicit/null pricing_provenance). Added ForgeConfig.model_registry_field_sources plus a check-config section naming which source supplied each field of an overlaid entry, and packaged the YAML explicitly via [tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel]. Docs updated in inputs-reference.md (new 'Model definitions' section) and model-reference.md (including the note that this repo's own forge.yaml migration is separate post-release operator work). New tests in tests/test_model_catalog.py (20) cover catalog loading, compatibility, expressiveness parity, adapter-validation errors, and field-level provenance including the check-config consumer.

handoff.summary: Iteration 2 addressed the single blocking P1: the [no_circular_imports] hard convention violation between theforge.config.models and theforge.config.model_catalog. The previous iteration relied on a deferred (function-level) import to make the cycle run, but the convention checker walks every import in the AST, and the back-edge was real regardless. Fixed structurally by extracting src/theforge/config/model_identity.py — a leaf module holding TransportSpec, RoutingPolicy, AgentSpec, transport_for plus the runner-derivation tables, the canonical-id helpers, the tier-derived routing defaults (custom_model_capability / custom_model_dev_capable), and the raw-input alias boundary (provider maps, provider_for_transport, transport_from_raw_fields, overlay_transport). It depends only on config/pricing.py (stdlib-only), so model_catalog.py and models.py both build on it and neither imports the other; models.py re-exports the entire identity surface with `as` aliases so every existing import site across src/ and tests/ is unaffected. models.py now loads the packaged catalog at module scope with no deferred import, and drops the eight dead _TRANSPORT_* constants that sat inside the moved block. Added a TestLayering class pinning that the parser does not import the registry, the leaf imports neither, and models.py still re-exports the identity names; recorded the intended import direction in config/CONVENTIONS.md. Verified with the project's own conventions checker against the pre-story baseline b532132: zero net-new circular-import, max_module_lines, or test_mirrors_source violations.

handoff.summary: Iteration 1 review fix. The P1 was that models.custom only accepted the legacy flat declaration shape, so a definition written in the canonical schema was rejected for missing flat fields — leaving the reusable declaration surface less expressive than an inline models.enabled mapping, which is exactly the split this story closes. Added _custom_definition() in config/load.py: it selects the shape from the legacy-only top-level keys (tier, input_cost_per_mtok, output_cost_per_mtok), routing a canonical declaration straight to the shared parse_definition and a flat one through the existing _custom_declaration_to_definition translation; a declaration carrying both shapes is rejected rather than resolved under one reading (config loading is an integrity boundary, and two spellings of tier would decide routing by guess). The `override` control key is stripped before parsing. Alias-key selection, provider alias tokens, adapter validation, and standalone (builtin=None) resolution semantics are unchanged on both paths. Also fixed the three in-scope P2s: deleted the now-dead _entry() and LOCAL_OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_BASE_URL from config/models.py (rewriting the two _entry() cases in test_pricing_provenance.py to drive the same #2203 attribution guard through parse_definition/resolve_packaged, where a shipped entry is really built), and corrected docs/guides/inputs-reference.md, whose identity section claimed no config names a runner while the canonical transport block accepts transport.runner — it now states the derivation rule plus the explicit-runner exception, and documents models.custom as a canonical definition surface. Four new tests cover the canonical models.custom path: accepted and selectable by key, override of a shipped identity, unsupported provider naming the adapters, and mixed-shape rejection.

findings.description: A project model written under models.custom in the canonical schema is rejected as missing legacy flat fields, so a fully expressive reusable declaration cannot be loaded outside models.enabled.
The identity section still says no config names a runner, while the canonical schema documented later accepts transport.runner.
The _entry() function is defined in models.py but never called after the refactoring; the AGENT_REGISTRY is now built by load_packaged_catalog() instead.

The LOCAL_OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_BASE_URL constant is defined but never used after refactoring; the URL was previously passed to _entry() for local-endpoint models, but is now hardcoded directly in models.yaml.

plan_review.findings:
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-opus-cli] Step 2 asserts the inline models.enabled nested routing/cost form is 'already fully expressive' and Step 1's field list omits pricing_provenance and cost_rank_basis. It is not expressive enough for the shipped set: config/models.py:_entry accepts both, and pricing.resolve_cost_band_basis (config/pricing.py:64-104) *raises* when a band is neither price-attributable nor explicitly based. Shipped entries such as the Anthropic sonnet/opus shorthands deliberately carry pricing_provenance=None with a declared non-price cost_rank_basis, while _parse_enabled_mapping_entry (load.py:283-290) hardcodes PRICING_PROVENANCE_OPERATOR_DECLARED for any declared cost: block — round-tripping the shipped set through that shape as-is would re-band shorthands off unattributed literals, the exact defect #2217 fixed. Not a blocker only because tests/test_pricing_provenance.py:110/117/128 pin AGENT_REGISTRY provenance and will fail immediately.
  Suggestion: Add explicit pricing_provenance and cost_rank_basis (nullable) to the canonical catalog schema in Step 1, and in Step 2 have the shared parser honor declared values instead of inferring operator-declared attribution; keep the operator-declared inference only on the legacy models.custom / inline compatibility paths.
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-opus-cli] Step 2 lists both config/models.py and config/load.py as homes for the shared canonical parser, but load.py already imports AGENT_REGISTRY from models.py — if the parser that builds AGENT_REGISTRY at import time lives in load.py, that is a circular import. Additionally, _parse_enabled_mapping_entry's semantics are overlay semantics: it consults AGENT_REGISTRY.get(canonical_id) for tier/capability/cost/base_url fallbacks (load.py:265-345), which cannot apply when the parser is what constructs AGENT_REGISTRY.
  Suggestion: Put the canonical parser in config/models.py (or a new leaf module both import) and split it into base parsing (no builtin fallback, used for packaged catalog) and overlay resolution (builtin-aware, used for project declarations).
- [P2] [anthropic-opus-cli] Step 5's file list names src/theforge/model_profiles.py and src/theforge/coordinator/model_profiles_bridge.py, neither of which references registry_source today; the file that actually holds the entry-level reporting surface — config/types.py, where ForgeConfig.model_registry_sources is declared at types.py:1241 — is not listed. The new field-level provenance map needs a ForgeConfig field there, and cli/check_config.py:464-469 is the existing consumer to keep working.
  Suggestion: Include config/types.py (ForgeConfig field) and cli/check_config.py in Step 5's scope; touch the model_profiles modules only if a concrete need surfaces.
- [P1-impl] [openai-gpt-5.4-cli] Step 2 says to use the current inline models.enabled nested routing/cost shape because it is 'already fully expressive', but the current shipped registry uses metadata that shape does not express today: pricing_provenance and routing.cost_rank_basis in src/theforge/config/models.py:_entry, while src/theforge/config/load.py:_parse_enabled_mapping_entry can only infer operator-declared pricing/banding. If implementation literally reuses the current inline shape unchanged, built-in entries like anthropic/sonnet, deepseek-reasoner, and local OpenAI-compatible models will lose existing routing/accounting semantics.
  Suggestion: Keep the shared-parser approach, but extend the canonical cost schema enough to round-trip current AgentSpec pricing/band metadata rather than treating the existing inline shape as sufficient as-is.
- [P2] [openai-gpt-5.4-cli] Backward-compat in Step 4 should explicitly preserve alias-key resolution for models.custom declarations. Current loader behavior lets models.enabled select a custom declaration by its operator-chosen key and then rewrites it to the canonical identity via _parse_custom_model_registry/overlay_aliases in src/theforge/config/load.py; tests rely on this (tests/test_config_transport_identity.py, tests/test_config_load.py).
  Suggestion: Call out declaration-key alias preservation in the compatibility adapter and add a focused test that models.enabled: ['gpt-5.5'] still resolves to openai/gpt-5.5/cli when declared under models.custom.

finding_registry.description: A project model written under models.custom in the canonical schema is rejected as missing legacy flat fields, so a fully expressive reusable declaration cannot be loaded outside models.enabled.
The identity section still says no config names a runner, while the canonical schema documented later accepts transport.runner.
The _entry() function is defined in models.py but never called after the refactoring; the AGENT_REGISTRY is now built by load_packaged_catalog() instead.

The LOCAL_OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_BASE_URL constant is defined but never used after refactoring; the URL was previously passed to _entry() for local-endpoint models, but is now hardcoded directly in models.yaml.

soft: Coordinator is pure Python — no LLM calls for routing or process decisions
Schema validation is the integrity boundary — do not relax cross-validation rules
Keep modules single-purpose; extract instead of growing monolith files
Keep pure-data types in low-dependency modules with stdlib-only imports
Separate prompt construction, output parsing, and coordinator control flow

When adding or modifying data that flows between coordinator phases, instrument the change so the actual values are visible in the audit trail — diagnosing sprint failures requires tracing real data, not reconstructing it
Do not create files outside src/, tests/, or docs/. If you need a scratch file for exploration, delete it before committing.

Changes that affect coordinator phase boundaries, state handoff between phases, or adaptive routing/config propagation must include seam-level integration tests covering the touched boundary. Unit tests alone are insufficient when correctness depends on cross-phase state flow.
